newsitem.title: USA: New York judge upholds workfare requirements-paper.
newsitem.headline: New York judge upholds workfare requirements-paper.

text.p: A New York Supreme Court judge in Manhattan has upheld Gov. George Pataki's workfare requirement for Home Relief recipients, New York Post reported Thursday.

Supreme Court Justice Harold Tompkins rejected a claim by 19-year old Sergio Ortiz that he was a full-time student and should not have to work to collect welfare benefits. The student had sued the city and state departments of social services last year after his aid was cut off.
The judge praised the workfare requirements. "The hallmark of the reformed welfare system is personal accountability," the Post quoting him as saying.
And the paper said State Attorney General Dennis Vacco hailed the decision, as it removes a threat to workfare programs.
"This ruling is crucial in allowing the reforms to go forward," Vacco told the Post.
Home Relief is a state-city funded program mainly for single, able-bodied adults.

In 1995, New York State imposed a requirement that Home Relief beneficiaries who are 19 years or older take part in workfare programs in order to get the aid. Only those who are younger than 19 and who are attending school are not obliged to work, the paper said.
